selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test the most impactful design choice: multimodal modeling. This configuration tests combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It directly addresses whether combining modalities improves performance compared to single-modality baselines, which is critical for prioritizing future exploration.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (config_017) improves performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether weighted fusion could yield better results than simple concatenation, a critical design choice with minimal other changes.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.525 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with the same encoders but avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, isolating the impact of profile setting. It balances exploration of multiprofile (a key design choice) while keeping encoders consistent, providing critical evidence on whether multiprofile improves performance without overcomplicating other factors.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile configurations with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_018) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_019) could further improve performance, isolating the effect of fusion method. It is the best next step as it directly compares two key design choices (fusion type) within a proven high-performing framework, balancing exploitation of current insights with exploration of critical components.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_019) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.6390). This experiment tests whether using a more sophisticated RNA encoder (scvi_n200) instead of pca_n2000 would further improve performance while keeping the promising setup of multiprofile, avgpool, and weighted fusion. This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, a critical design choice, and builds on the strong foundation of the current best configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced image encoder) further improves performance while keeping other parameters constant, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_037) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.706). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more advanced model) and using transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) could further improve performance. It isolates the impact of the RNA encoder and aggregation method, which are critical design choices, while keeping the image encoder and fusion strategy consistent. This balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of key variables.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models (e.g., config_037) outperform single-modality models, but uncertainty remains about whether RNA-only models could match or exceed performance with better encoders. This experiment tests a simple RNA-only baseline (pca_n2000 encoder, singleprofile) to isolate the impact of modality. It clarifies whether RNA data alone can achieve competitive accuracy, which is critical for understanding if multimodal fusion is necessary. This is the best use of the next experiment as it addresses a key design choice (modality) with minimal changes, avoiding overfitting to complex interactions.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more advanced model) maintains or improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. It builds on the current best configuration while exploring a critical design decision with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation while maintaining weighted fusion isolates the effect of aggregation method. It directly addresses a key design choice with potential to improve performance without altering other critical parameters.
